text.p: Turkish central bank heavily funded banks through overnight, tomorrow/next and tomorrow/week value deals to relieve cash shortage on Tuesday and sold dollars for lira to curb persistent year-end demand for the U.S currency, bankers said.

It lent 31.7 trillion lira overnight at 78 percent, 23.5 trillion lira t/n at 74 percent and 2.9 trillion lira t/w at 75 percent. On Monday, it had funded 32.5 trillion lira via t/n and 1.1 trillion lira via t/w at the same rates.

The bank intervened in the dollar and the lira firmed to 106,740 against the dollar from a low of 106,930 before the intervention. It had opened weaker at 106,780, versus Monday's 106,560 as banks continued to buy dollars to close their currency positions ahead of the year-end.
Bankers said dollar demand by was also on the rise, usual for the year-end.
They said the central bank intervention came after minor fluctuation in the lira/dollar rates ahead of the results of a Treasury auction.

"There was a mild fluctuation in lira/dollar rates in early afternoon as some banks sold dollars. But the lira again weakened to below 106,900, prompting central bank intervention," said a private banker.
Bankers said the market was cautious since the opening amid expectations of dollar sales by the central bank after last week's three rounds of intervention.
The treasury sold only 69.275 trillion lira worth 392-day bonds at the auction, raising the yield by 1.78 points to 125.45 percent from the previous 392-day auction held on December 17.

Most t-bill and bond yields fell ahead of the auction results on expectations of lower yield in the auction. But the yield on the January 14, 1998 paper, the nearest maturity to January 21, 1998 bonds sold in the auction, firmed to 112.00 percent from Monday's 111.38.
The most heavily traded June 4, 1997 paper yielded 111.93 percent, down from Monday's 113.40.
Banks will pay 28.2 trillion lira to the Treasury for the auction on Wednesday when 133.8 trillion lira t-bills will mature.

A net surplus of more than 70 trillion lira will be left idle after banks repay today's overnight borrowing to the central bank. Another 23.5 trillion lira will enter the market from today's t/n borrowing.
